fatal_errors: The cited evidence concerns fusion-reactor materials and provides no support for Zr-enhanced glass formation or thermal stability in transition-metal–phosphorus alloys.
The proposed intervention does not reconstruct the demonstrated Fe/Co/Mn adjustment and phosphorus reduction to 15 at.%, nor the associated shift toward eutectic-dominated solidification.
No alloy-specific evidence establishes that 3 at.% Zr will form favorable eutectics, avoid Zr-rich phosphides or intermetallics, or increase stability in this P-rich composition.
Cooling and reheating conditions are not quantitatively specified, preventing comparison with the demonstrated approximately 20 micrometer ribbon, 40 m/s melt spinning, and 20 K/min DSC conditions.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general objective and proposes a testable control-versus-Zr experiment using appropriate structural and thermal measurements. Its generic size-mismatch and nucleation-barrier mechanism is scientifically conceivable, but it is not substantiated for this alloy and does not match the target intervention or eutectic/partitioning mechanism. The boundaries are vague and include the questionable suggestion that excessively rapid heating would promote crystallization; faster heating commonly shifts apparent crystallization to higher temperature or can help bypass crystallization. The falsification threshold is also poorly defined: a 10% increase in absolute crystallization temperature would be an unusually large requirement, while the use of 'and/or' makes rejection ambiguous. Most importantly, the sole citation is wholly irrelevant, so this remains an unsupported alternative rather than an evidence-based plausible reconstruction.
